text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Mayor of Croat-held southern town of Stolac accused Moslems, who were expelled from area in 1992 and now want to return, of provocating and insulting domestic Croat population during their recent visits.
- Serb member of Bosnian Presidency criticized a number of Bosnian ambassadors for acting as representatives of Moslem people and not of whole Bosnian population.

- In view of the current political circumstances in Bosnia, is there a need for a Third Bosniaks (Moslem) meeting to be held to determine future of Moslem nation and state of Bosnia, the paper asks in a commentary.
- (Croat) president of the Bosnian Federation asks for a Croat to be Prime Minister of the Federation Government.
- Status of northern town of Brcko will be solved in December, Moslem member of arbitration commission says.
- The paper reported, citing World Health Organisation sources, that foreign donors delivered to Bosnia 810 tonnes of drugs that had passed their expiry date.
